answer: Each identity must forge a non-shareable sequential memory proof over a dedicated 16 GB working set that mixes a sable salt into every step of a dune-shaped hash chain. The verifier replays a random 2 MB slice against the epoch seed and rejects any timing or collision that reveals shared RAM. One honest agent runs the proof on a single 600-dollar machine in under 40 s; a farm of 150 clones must buy 150 separate machines and 2.4 TB of RAM because the live working set cannot be pooled or swapped. Failed proofs slash a 20 POA bond and freeze the cluster for two epochs.
